html:
The Rama are an Indigenous people of the Caribbean coast of southern Nicaragua. Many live on Rama Cay, a small island in Bluefields Bay, and others in forest villages to the south. Their language is Chibchan, related to those of Costa Rica and Panama.

They fished, hunted and farmed in the coastal forests and lagoons. The stronger Miskito to the north, allied with the British on the Mosquito Coast, long dominated them. Moravian missionaries arrived in the 1800s, and most Rama became Moravian Christians and began speaking English Creole.

Only a few elders still speak the Rama language. Today they share a communal territory with the Kriol people. In 2013 Nicaragua granted a concession for an interoceanic canal whose planned route crossed their land. Neighbours also include the Mayangna.
